subject: Re: Crestline Labs — token velocity, peak TPS & $/1M target (post-demo recap)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ari Johnson <ari@crestlinelabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Crestline Labs — token velocity, peak TPS & $/1M target (post-demo recap)

Hi Ari — thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can lock the hosted pricing for the pilot: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct me if I’ve mis-typed):
- Primary workload: user-facing summarization and policy-checks on clinical notes (mix of short and long inputs).
- Expected steady-state: ~18–30M tokens / month across the initial pilot (Q4), with distribution skewed toward business hours in US-Eastern.
- Peak behavior: regular daytime peaks and occasional product launches where traffic can spike 6–8x for ~10–30 minute windows. You estimated an observed peak of ~120 TPS during last launch.
- Quality target: match or exceed current on-prem baseline; you flagged that latency at 99th percentile must stay under 450ms for the user-facing summarize flow.

Pricing constraints you called out:
- Target dollar-per-1M-tokens: $600–$850 (internal budget band).
- Procurement prefers a single hosted SKU for simplicity but is open to a small reserve (dedicated burst) if it helps with 99th latency.

Open questions for us before we put together a formal estimate:
1) Confirm the monthly token range we should price: is the lower bound 18M or should we model a conservative 12M for month-1?
2) For peak sizing: can you share an anonymized 1-hour request sample or a CSV with per-minute TPS for the largest spike you referenced? That will help us size autoscaling and the 99th-tps bucket.
3) Any constraint on retention/PII that would require Private (VPC) vs. Hosted? You mentioned Crestline’s clinical team prefers data-in-hosted for the pilot but procurement may insist on additional audit logs.

Next steps from our side: I’ll assemble a simple hosted-rate estimate with two options — (A) hosted-only with a $/1M tiered slab and autoscaling guardrails, and (B) hosted + small reserved burst (monthly commit + burst pool) to guarantee 99th latency under 450ms. I’ll attach the draft estimate and a mutual action plan for signatures.

Attachments: crestline_estimate_v1.pdf (draft pricing), crestline_map_v2.xlsx (MAP draft)

Can you get back to us on Q1–Q2 above by EOD Tuesday (PST)? If easier, we can do a short 20-min follow-up tomorrow.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ari Johnson <ari@crestlinelabs.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@crestline.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Crestline Labs — token velocity, peak TPS & $/1M target (post-demo recap)

Thanks Mateo — useful recap. A few clarifications below: 

Quick answers:
- Monthly baseline: please price for 15–28M tokens for month 1–3. That reflects ramp from beta to GA; 18M is our optimistic median, 15M is the conservative low.
- Peak sample: attached a one-hour CSV from our biggest launch last quarter (per-minute TPS). The peak minute hit 138 TPS; sustained peaks were ~85–100 TPS for ~12 minutes. (Attachment: crestline_spike_202605.csv)
- Data controls: for pilot we are OK with hosted so long as we get audit logs and a 30-day access log retention policy. Procurement will confirm if additional controls are needed for GA.

Budget band: procurement confirmed the $/1M target is $600 preferred; they may accept up to $800 if we can justify a guaranteed 99th latency and a short-term price cap for the first 3 months.

A couple of asks before we sign the MAP: 
- Can Redwood guarantee the 99th latency SLO under the ‘hosted + small reserved burst’ option for the TPS profile in the attached CSV? If so, we’ll aim to include a 60-day SLA clause.
- Please model an estimate that includes a ‘spike credit’ — a small burst pool that covers up to 20 minutes of 6x traffic without immediate overage charge (we’ll accept a one-time mitigation credit).

Happy to hop on 20 mins tomorrow — 11:00–11:30am ET works (I’ll book if you confirm).

Best,
Ari
VP Product & Ops | Crestline Labs
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ari Johnson <ari@crestlinelabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@crestline.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Crestline Labs — token velocity, peak TPS & $/1M target (post-demo recap)

Ari — perfect, thanks for the CSV and clear guidance. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) Pricing model (deliverable by EOD 2026-08-19):
   - Option A (Hosted, tiered slab): $/1M = $820 at 0–15M, $700 at 15–40M, $620 at 40M+. No reserved capacity. Autoscaling with soft throttles; 99th latency expectation ~600–800ms on biggest spikes.
   - Option B (Hosted + small reserved burst): baseline $/1M = $680 constant slab for 15–40M with a 100k-token/month reserved burst pool (applied as credit). With conservative kernel selection and burst pool, we can target 99th latency < 450ms for the sample spike shape you shared. This includes a 60-day latency credit clause for the pilot (details in attached PDF).

2) Operational controls: we’ll enable audit logs with 30-day retention and provide an export link to your security team. If procurement requires longer retention, we can scope Private deployment for GA.

3) MAP & procurement: I attached the revised estimate (crestline_estimate_v1.pdf) and an updated MAP with milestones (crestline_map_v2.xlsx). Please review and mark any redlines.

4) Follow-up call: confirm 11:00–11:30am ET tomorrow and we’ll walk procurement through Option B and the latency SLO language.

Action items for Ari / Crestline:
- Confirm the 15M lower bound for month-1 pricing (reply-all).
- Procurement: indicate whether a 30-day audit log retention is sufficient or if you need 90 days (procurement@crestline.com).
- If you want us to model a slightly larger burst pool (200k tokens) we can update Option B and show incremental cost impact.

I’ll loop in our technical lead if we get the go-ahead to finalize SLO wording. Thanks — looking forward to closing this pilot.

Best regards,
Mateo
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: crestline_estimate_v1.pdf, crestline_map_v2.xlsx
